report.source_text: Lymph node biopsy revealed diffuse infiltration of small to medium-sized lymphocytes with rare nuclear irregularities, which distorted the nodal architecture. Giant cells with irregularly lobulated nuclei, like Reed-Sternberg cells, were scattered among the background lymphocytes (Fig. 1). Some macrophages and angiogenesis were also observed. On immunohistochemical analysis, the giant cells were positive for CD30 and CD15, and negative for CD3, CD20, PAX5, and Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA1 in situ hybridization (EBER-ISH). The background lymphocytes were positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD25 (partially). These findings were consistent with lymphocyte-rich classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man with a history of HAM/TSP and HTLV-1 positivity presented with right inguinal lymphadenopathy. Initial blood work showed high soluble IL-2 receptor levels. A biopsy of the lymph node revealed diffuse infiltration of small to medium-sized lymphocytes with Reed-Sternberg-like giant cells, positive for CD30 and CD15, and negative for CD3, CD20, PAX5, and EBER-ISH. Background lymphocytes were positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD25, leading to an initial interpretation consistent with lymphocyte-rich classic Hodgkin lymphoma. However, subsequent Southern blot analysis detected di-clonal proviral HTLV-1 DNA bands in both the lymph node and peripheral blood samples. This finding, in conjunction with the Hodgkin-like features, confirmed the diagnosis of Hodgkin-like ATLL (lymphoma type). During follow-up, atypical lymphoid cells appeared in the peripheral blood, and soluble IL-2 receptor levels temporarily increased.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with right inguinal lymphadenopathy and had a history of HTLV-1 infection (HAM/TSP) and positive anti-HTLV-1 antibody.
Blood examination revealed a high soluble interleukin (IL)-2 receptor level of 1000 U/L and positivity of anti-HTLV-1 antibody (ELISA and western blotting assay).

Lymph node biopsy showed diffuse infiltration of small to medium-sized lymphocytes with Reed-Sternberg-like giant cells, positive for CD30 and CD15, and negative for CD3, CD20, PAX5, and EBER-ISH. Background lymphocytes were positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD25 (partially).
Di-clonal proviral HTLV-1 DNA bands were detected in the lymph node and peripheral blood samples on Southern blot analysis.
Appearance of atypical lymphoid cells (maximum: 160/µl) in the peripheral blood and a temporary increase in soluble IL-2 receptor level (maximum: 2018 U/L) during follow-up.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Although initial lymph node pathology findings were consistent with lymphocyte-rich cHL (Reed-Sternberg-like cells, CD30+, CD15+, EBER-ISH negative), the detection of di-clonal proviral HTLV-1 DNA in the lymph node (E004) in an HTLV-1 positive patient makes cHL less likely and points towards an HTLV-1 associated lymphoproliferative disorder with Hodgkin-like features.
